### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **200** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**89** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `userId (5 routes)`
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 53 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 53 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 53 pages)`
- **22** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `812414b66fe6fcfa1a6eebec505465ea34e58ba1` — the merge of head `84a7069f3fc371157db6d470bb0f6f49178a0cc4` into base `199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 812414b66fe6fcfa1a6eebec505465ea34e58ba1 && git checkout 812414b66fe6fcfa1a6eebec505465ea34e58ba1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb 84a7069f3fc371157db6d470bb0f6f49178a0cc4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb && git merge --no-ff 84a7069f3fc371157db6d470bb0f6f49178a0cc4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f5a084c771de8823e3fd0a872640441e0518a57f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user-identity-source-label.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-ban-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-database-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.conformance.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-route-ledger.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/cloud-managed.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/environment-user-host.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/implicit-account-linking.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/password-reset-ends-sessions.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-marker.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-seams.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/pending-sso-users.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/service-account-identity.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/set-initial-password.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/user-ban-write.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/user-session-admission.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-platform-admin-standing.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-route-nonadmin-refusal.dogfood.test.ts + .changeset/33181-pending-sso-users.md, content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx

Inputs: card #33181 body and all 8 comments, PR #33227 body and its 51-file list, the net diff against `main` at this head, and the head's check-runs. Cited code outside the diff was read, not reviewed: `sso-only-local-password.ts`, `last-admin-guard.ts`, `stampIdentitySource` in `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts`, `packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`, and better-auth 1.7.12's `email-verification`, `magic-link` and `email-otp` routes.

Check-runs when read (54 total):
- success: Check Changeset (both runs), PR-body guards (both runs), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Auto Label, filter, Plan Test Core shards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Build Docs, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger.
- in progress: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus.
- failed: none. The rest are skipped.
- This verdict is a design verdict. The in-progress runs remain the gate verdicts, and the PR does not land before they conclude.

### ① Derived judgments

- Narrowing, declared, right: `admin/ban-user` now works without the admin plugin, and a banned row is refused a session. `admin/unban-user` lifts it there too. The admission runs only when `isAdminPluginMounted()` is false, so a kernel with the plugin is untouched.
- Widening, declared, right:
  - `POST /admin/add-sso-user` and `POST /admin/import-sso-users`, platform-admin gated first, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` off a managed environment.
  - The `idp_pending` option of `sys_user.source`.
  - The `environmentUserHost` option and `AuthManager#isAdminPluginMounted()`.
  - The exports of `pending-sso-marker`, `environment-user-host` and `pending-sso-users`.
  - The audit event `user.admin_added_pending`, two route-ledger rows and two dogfood sweep entries.
- Widening, not declared, wrong (should-fix 1): `index.ts` re-exports `admin-user-endpoints.js`, `set-initial-password.js` and `admin-ban-endpoints.js` with `export *`. The diff therefore publishes `bindUserToSoleOrganization`, `writeAdminAudit`, `CreationRefused`, `joinCurrentOrganization`, `multiOrgCreationJoinsCurrentOrganization`, `AdminAuditDecisions`, `SetInitialPasswordOptions` with the third parameter of `runSetInitialPassword`, and three new optional members of `AdminBanEndpointDeps`. The `Clause-②:` line names none of them.
- New `409` for a pending row at `set-user-password`, `set-initial-password`, `/reset-password` and `/phone-number/reset-password`: right, and it narrows nothing, since no row carries the marker on `main`. The four doors are the same set `sso-only-local-password.ts` names as every door that writes a hash without proving a current one.
- `resolveResetDoorUserId` now runs on both reset doors in every mode, where it ran only in SSO-only mode: right. The read spends nothing, swallows its own faults, and a `{ ok: false }` answer is ignored outside SSO-only mode.
- `readSessionUserRow` replacing `refuseAgentAccountSession`'s body: right. Same guards, same read fault, same refusal; the old entry point is kept.
- The four cloud-managed `409` sentences: right, final per decision 6878953650.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — matches the tree. One arm from the closed pair, with the BREAKING banner in both the PR body and the changeset.

- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` is the level AGENTS.md gives a non-protocol change, breaking or not.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: `sys_user.source` is a system-managed column of a platform object, not something a metadata author writes.
- The ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is present, and nothing stored needs rewriting.
- Both Check Changeset runs concluded success.
- The declaration line is incomplete on the widened side (should-fix 1).

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question, the provisional `409` wording: answered by decision 6878953650.
- Cancel-on-delete door, durable outbox with retry, per-row invitation status (execution terms, 6870710213): not in this PR, deferred to #33228 as the release comment 6872883193 states. Accepted as a named follow-up. Until it lands, a host failure has no retry other than the administrator repeating the call.
- Console entry and `requiresFeature: 'admin'` on the `sys_user` ban actions: deferred to #33186. Accepted.
- "Adding an email that already has an environment row: decide in child 1a": decided. A pending row answers `200 alreadyPending` and re-tells the host; any other row answers `409`. See should-fix 4 for what the re-add drops.
- Escalated to the maintainer (should-fix 2): the term "An owner or admin 409 refuses the whole deactivation" holds only while the host answers. A host that throws anything but a typed refusal lets the ban go ahead. That is the seat's choice in 6869729952, made before the rulings were quoted on the card.
- Escalated (should-fix 5): the term "attributed through the handoff's `by`" has no carrier in the event. `actorCloudUserId` is always read from the session user's own linked account.
- "Console-side removal: the roster shows that state" is not this child's surface; no finding.

### ④ Design judgment

A row of the new files per contract sentence, then the findings.

- `pending-sso-marker.ts`, `sys-user.object.ts` and its label test: hold. The marker is its own value, never `env_native`, as the execution terms require.
- `pending-sso-users.ts`: holds for the insert, the grants, the host call and the take-back.
  - The row is born pending in one engine insert, so there is no `env_native` moment.
  - Grants run under the caller's own context (ruling 2).
  - The host is called outside the unit of work (no transaction across the invite call).
  - A typed refusal takes the person back out, children first.
  - Findings 3, 4, 6 and 7 are here.
- `user-session-admission.ts`, `auth-manager-database-hooks.ts`, `service-account-identity.ts`: hold. One read per session, `503` on a read fault. Findings 3 and 8.
- `admin-ban-endpoints.ts`, `user-ban-write.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`, `auth-plugin.ts`: hold for writer selection, the closed field map and the self-ban refusal. The host is asked before the write. Findings 2, 5, 9 and 10.
- `auth-manager-before-hook.ts`, `admin-user-endpoints.ts`, `set-initial-password.ts`: the pending arms hold. A source that cannot be read falls through to the existing arms. The PR declares this, and it departs from the fail-closed convention of `sso-only-local-password.ts`. Accepted as a declared deviation; its one consequence is in finding 3.
- `implicit-account-linking.ts` (header only), `cloud-managed.ts`, `environment-user-host.ts`, `index.ts`, the ledger and its conformance list, the two dogfood tables, the two appended test files: agree with the code. `environment-user-host.ts` carries findings 5 and 10.

Findings:

1. should-fix — undeclared public exports (see ①), `index.ts:86-88` and `admin-user-endpoints.ts:478, 525, 607, 953, 980, 1023`. Name them on the `Clause-②:` line in the PR body and the changeset, or stop publishing the helpers.
2. should-fix, escalated — `environment-user-host.ts:175, 192` with `admin-ban-endpoints.ts:265`. A host that is unreachable cannot say whether the person is an organization owner or admin, and the deactivation proceeds. Ruling 5 says such a person "cannot be removed from the environment side". Either fail closed on `deactivated` when a host is wired and does not answer, or record the maintainer's word that fail-open stands.
3. should-fix — the pending marker clears only through `stampIdentitySource`, which is fail-soft and runs once.
   - It runs only in `account.create.after`, catches every error, and logs that "the sign-in is fine".
   - If that one write fails, the account link exists, the row still reads `idp_pending`, and `user-session-admission.ts:105` refuses the session.
   - Later sign-ins create no account, so the stamp never re-runs.
   - The stamp also skips a row that holds a credential account, which the declared read-fault fall-through can produce.
   - No door in this PR clears the marker, so the person is locked out.
   - Fix: let admission admit and stamp a pending row that already holds an `objectstack-cloud` account, or make a failed stamp on a pending row fail the link.
4. should-fix — `pending-sso-users.ts:343` and the second pass at `:633`. Re-adding a pending person answers `ok` with `alreadyPending` and drops the positions, permission sets and manager sent with it. Neither the answer nor `authentication.mdx` says so, so a corrected CSV reads as applied. Say what was not applied, on the row and in the docs, or apply it.
5. should-fix — `admin-ban-endpoints.ts:167` and `pending-sso-users.ts:426`. Under an impersonation session `actor.id` is the impersonated administrator, and the event carries their cloud id; `actor.impersonatedBy` is dropped. Ruling 3 attributes each invitation to the acting administrator. Carry `impersonatedBy` on the event; the handoff's `by` needs the same slot.
6. should-fix — `pending-sso-users.ts:618`. The import's per-row catch answers the raw thrown message of any fault, driver text included. The single-add door answers the generic `INTERNAL_ERROR_MESSAGE` for the same fault. Use the generic sentence for an undeclared 5xx.
7. One should-fix was reported privately.
8. nit — `user-session-admission.ts`: the expired-ban lift writes no `updated_at`, and a failed lift surfaces as an unshaped error.
9. nit — `admin-ban-endpoints.ts:265`: the host is asked before the write. If the write is then refused (the engine's last-administrator guard) or faults, the host has acted and the door answers `500` with no `host` field. Repeating the call recovers it. This belongs with the outbox on #33228.
10. nit — three comments disagree with the code:
    - `auth-plugin.ts:385-387`: the `environmentUserHost` jsdoc says the host is told "after the operation has committed" and "never undoes the operation". The ban and unban doors ask before the write, and a typed refusal does undo an add.
    - `environment-user-host.ts:46`: `occurredAt` is described as the time the operation committed.
    - `auth-plugin.ts:4059`: "a session that predates the marker" describes a state a born-pending row cannot have.
11. nit — a re-add that re-tells the host writes no audit row. `manager_id` names a column that holds an email address.

No must-fix. Findings 1 to 7 each earn a delta review of their fix.
